SCHOOLS IN JACKSON COUNTY
The first organized school in Kansas was organized in Wyandotte by J.M.
Armstrong in 1844. It lasted until his death in 1852. The school had the distinction of being the first
established for white children in what is now the state of Kansas. A school for whites was established in
Council Grove in 1851 byMr. T.S. Huffaker. The State of Kansas is challenged to find another county
surpassing Jackson in its zealous devotion to educational matters.
Shortly after the county was organized in 1857, the people began to think about schools for their children.
The first school was taught in this county by Miss Hariet Warfield of Clay County Missouri in 1857. It was
gotten up on the subscription plan, and held in a little log cabin, 10 feet square, located on the SW 1/4 section
23, township 9, range 16. This would put about 5 miles east of Hoyt. (1)
School was started in Jefferson township the same year. Mrs. H.S. Hart held school in her log cabin.
Hard times, drought, the coming of the Civil War and the internal strife in Kansas kept the people of Jackson
County from doing much about schools until after 1861. (1)
The first real school was built in the county in 1858. It was built out of logs and was also used as a church.
Information from the Kansas State Historical Society, says that the lighting came from leaving out one log in
the wall on one side. It was heated by a fireplace. It was taught by Miss Anna Parrot. The name of it was called
Brick, and was also the first organized district in county. Permission for this was granted on June 20, 1859. It
was located on land which was part of the Pottawatomie Reserve. The school term was six months, three
months in spring and three in the fall.
In 1868, George and Mary Hafer donated one acre of land to the school. It was about 1/2 mile west of the log
cabin. In the same Brick school was built. In one porch was W.H. Webster. He taught for seven terms. At
one time there were 58 students. The building was also used as a church until a church building was
completed in 1890. In 1916 the second building was torn down and a building, with a basement was erected.
School was held here until it was destroyed by a tornado in 1962. The last teacher was Katherin Linehan.
(The information about Brick was Kansas Historical Society and Forest Morris family and the Everett Gibson
family.)
